title: What are self-replicating ‘AI worms’, and why is Anthropic worried about them?
summary: The tech company says successful AI worms need more capability on less powerful devices, but current trends make that feasible by the end of the year Warnings about what artificial intelligence might do in the future – together with alarming reports of what it has gotten up to already – are being issued so quickly that even security experts have difficulty triaging what to worry about. Yet a report this week from Anthropic’s offensive research team grabbed attention by describing a new, practical threat, one devoid of human characteristics or apocalyptic musings. The red team, as such internal testers are called, said it created a malicious AI program that spread autonomously through internet-connected “smart” televisions and could do the same inside other ordinary devices. While machines running AI usually need a fair amount of computing power, the researchers said that their program split parts of itself among 15 televisions and was still able to function by using a bit of power from each. Continue reading...
title_en: Anthropic Warns of Self-Replicating AI Worms Spreading Across Smart Devices
title_zh: Anthropic警告可自我复制的AI蠕虫正蔓延于智能设备
summary_en: Anthropic's red team built a malicious AI program that spread autonomously across 15 smart TVs, splitting itself to run on limited power from each device, and warns such AI worms could become feasible by year-end.
summary_zh: Anthropic红队创建了一个恶意AI程序，可在15台智能电视间自主传播，通过拆分自身利用各设备有限算力运行，并警告此类AI蠕虫年底前或成现实。

title: TinyFish Makes Search Free: What It Really Costs an AI Agent to Read the Web
summary: An AI agent that reads the web pays 2 kinds of cost. The first is the retrieval charge: what a search or fetch API bills per request. The second is model processing: content passed from retrieved pages into an AI model consumes tokens, while reasoning and generated responses add further costs. TinyFish, a web infrastructure […] The post TinyFish Makes Search Free: What It Really Costs an AI Agent to Read the Web appeared first on MarkTechPost .
title_en: TinyFish Makes Search Free: What It Really Costs an AI Agent to Read the Web
title_zh: TinyFish 让搜索免费：AI 智能体读取网页的真实成本
summary_en: TinyFish offers free web search for AI agents, but reading the web still costs: retrieval charges per request plus token costs when retrieved content is processed by models, with reasoning and responses adding more.
summary_zh: TinyFish 为 AI 智能体提供免费网页搜索，但读取网页仍有成本：检索请求费用，以及内容传入模型时的 token 消耗，推理与生成响应还会增加开销。

Research、TEL、KLA、北方华创、中微公司、ASM、新凯来工业机器、Merck、盛美半导体、拓荆科技、SCREEN、DISCO、电科装备、华天科技、华海清科等海内外代表企业悉数登场，产业全链一展尽览。 全新设立的AIE 35mΩ及1200V 60mΩ两大产品，精准匹配OBC、悬架电控、车载DC-DC功率需求；拓荆科技推出 NF-300M Flowable Carbon可流动碳膜沉积技术与设备；中微公司重点推介最新高端半导体微观加工设备——Primo XD-RIE™极高深宽比刻蚀设备与Prefima Unicore™ AM MOSFET系列芯片及DeepXETM嵌入式PCB功率模块，并针对AI数据中心领域发布基于成熟量产芯片PG4E的单管系列及EZ2C/3C特色模块家族，用先进碳化硅技术重新定义能源效率边界......一系列首发创新成果清晰勾勒设备、材料、工艺与应用之间的产业协同脉络，全景展现我国半导体技术持续迭代升级、加速自主可控的坚实步伐。 不一样的“芯”智汇 高端对话共探前沿 不一样的“芯”答卷 供需携手产业共进 2026湾芯展市场化对接成效显著，定向邀约华虹半导体、粤芯半导体、积塔半导体、长江存储、武汉新芯、晶合集成、长鑫存储、士兰微等43家Fab核心晶圆制造企业开展洽谈，累计吸引超6500位专业采购商到场。围绕企业寻源、技术合作与项目发展需求，本届展会面向采购、工艺及产线运维等环节，组织开展近50场供应链、投融资及采购对接活动，一批战略合作与协同创新项目落地。深圳平湖实验室与20家产业链伙伴完成战略合作签约，共建化合物半导体产学研用创新生态；CHIPX携手天通股份、六芯光电、Luceda等产业链上下游企业依托国内首条光子芯片中试线开放晶圆级制造与流片服务，深化工艺研发、技术验证及产业应用等环节协同合作，推动光子芯片关键技术与产业需求深度对接；图灵量子与深圳市智城算网科技有限公司、亚洲算力算网与量子计算科技有限公司正式签署战略合作协议，打造粤港澳量超智异构算力平台；硅芯科技联合迈特芯、华润微、华南理工大学、广东工业大学等10余家单位正式发起设立大湾区3D 从展会的“高人气”到产业的“强磁场”，以湾芯展为纽带，粤港澳大湾区半导体产业正以更开放的姿态融入全球创新网络，持续为全球产业贡献“中国方案”与“湾区实践”。

title_en: 2026 WESEMiBAY Semiconductor Expo Concludes Successfully in Shenzhen
title_zh: 2026湾芯展圆满落幕：3天展期，近8万平方米展区迎来超15.67万人次专业观众
summary_en: The 2026 WESEMiBAY expo in Shenzhen drew over 156,700 visitors across nearly 80,000 square meters, with 1,000+ exhibitors from 20+ countries and 3,000+ new products, spanning wafer manufacturing, compound semiconductors, advanced packaging, and AI infrastructure.
summary_zh: 2026湾芯展在深圳闭幕，3天展期近8万平方米，吸引超15.67万人次专业观众、20余国1000余家企业参展，首发新品超3000件，覆盖晶圆制造、化合物半导体、先进封装与AI基础设施。
